subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

__Despite play__ very well, we lost the match.
solution:
The correct answer is "**despite playing**". 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**Play**" is used in **simple present tense** if the noun in **plural**. The noun in the given sentence is **singular**. 
 
• "**Playing**" is in the **continuous tense** which shows an **on going action**.
 
• To justify the **subject verb concord **in the given sentence, **continuous tense** must be used because during the match, playing was going on, that is, it was continuous. .
 
• Therefore, the option "despite playing" is appropriate. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The three basic types of tenses are **present, past and future.**
 
• **Present tense** - denotes the action happening **now**.
 
 
• **Example**: *Nancy **eats** a sandwich. *
 
 
 
• **Past tense** - denotes an action already **happened**. 
 
 
• **Example**: *Nancy **ate** a sandwich yesterday. *
 
 
 
• **Future tense** - denotes an action that is **yet to happen**.
 
 
• **Example:** *Nancy **will eat** her sandwich after an hour.*
 
 
 
• All these tenses are further divided as **simple, continuous, perfect and perfect continuous.**
